Privacy notice

Draft — pending review by counsel. This notice describes what the current code does; it has not yet been reviewed by a lawyer. The name of the operator and a contact address are still to be added.

Draft dated November 13, 2026.

In short

  • You can use the map, forecasts and downloads without an account.
  • If you make an account, we store what you save in it, and you can export or delete all of it yourself.
  • We do not use advertising or third-party tracking scripts.
  • We do not sell your information.

Your account

You sign in with a passkey. There is no password, and we do not ask for or store an email address, phone number or real name. You can give the account a display name (up to 60 characters); that is optional. We store your passkey’s public key and its use count and dates, never the private key.

When you sign in, we keep a record of that sign-in with the first 80 characters of your browser’s description (for example “Chrome on Mac”) so you can see where you are signed in and sign out other devices. We set one cookie, __Host-sc_session, when you sign in. It keeps you signed in for 30 days from your last use and is not used for tracking.

What an account stores, and for how long

What Why How long
Account id, display name, passkeys To sign you in No automatic deletion found. Kept until you delete your account.
Sign-in sessions To keep you signed in; list your devices Until they expire (30 days after last use) or you sign out.
Saved trips and their settings (area, forecast point, species, date, hours, limits, boat, plan) To check the forecast and send alerts Removed 90 days after the trip date, or when you delete them.
Alerts we sent you and delivery records To show alert history and avoid sending twice 90 days.
Notification devices (your browser’s push address and keys; up to 5) To deliver alerts Until you turn notifications off, the push service reports the device gone, or you delete your account.
Comfort ratings To tune comfort estimates 365 days.
Private catch log (time, method, species, outcome, count, optional position and note) Your own record No automatic deletion found. Kept until you delete the entry or your account.
Saved spots (name, position, optional note; up to 100) Your own private places No automatic deletion found. Kept until you delete the spot or your account.

Your catch log and saved spots are private to your account. No public page, feed or other account reads them. Positions are optional in the catch log and required for a saved spot. They are stored on our server only if you press Save. “Use my position” asks your browser for one location when you press it. Backups: deleted records may remain in database backups kept by our hosting provider for a time.

Export and delete

In the trip-alerts panel, “Export my records” downloads your trips, ratings, alerts, devices (push service name and date only), catch log and saved spots, and your account details as one JSON file. “Delete account” (account panel) or “Delete all my records” (trip-alerts panel) removes all of that at once, including your passkeys and sessions. It cannot be undone, and there is no waiting period. To correct a record, change or delete it and save it again.

Boat lookup (AI)

The boat lookup is not available yet.

Usage statistics

We do not collect usage statistics. Our pages are built to send a small set of anonymous counts to our own Cloudflare analytics dataset, not to an analytics company, but at present the server discards them and stores none. If storing is ever switched on, this notice will be updated first. What the counts would be:

  • Visit steps, once per page load and region, with the region, the site build and, where the link had one, whether the visit came from a text, Instagram, Facebook or our printed QR code. The map sends map_viewed, port_selected, spot_saved and offline_saved. The home page sends error reports only.
  • Error reports when a page hits an uncaught error: the message with web-address queries, positions, emails and long numbers removed and cut short, the script’s file name only, and the site build.
  • Server counts: each request to our server by page type, method, status and speed, without your IP address, account, or what you typed.

There is no cookie, no storage and no visitor, session or device id in these counts. If your browser sends Do Not Track or Global Privacy Control, the pages send neither visit steps nor error reports.

On your device

Your home port, boat profile, comfort limits, language, map choices, a private map log (up to 500 entries, including positions you pick on the map) and saved offline map data are kept in your browser’s storage and never sent to us. Clearing your browser’s site data removes them.

Other companies that see your visit

Our site runs on Cloudflare, which handles your IP address and requests to deliver and secure it. Our host keeps standard request logs. Your browser loads map tiles and public data directly from OpenStreetMap, NOAA (weather, tides, charts, cloud imagery), the National Weather Service, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (protected-area boundaries via ArcGIS), the U.S. Geological Survey (aerial imagery) and GitHub (backup copies of data files). Each sees your IP address under its own policy. Alerts are delivered through your browser’s push service (Google, Mozilla, Apple or Microsoft).

Changes and contact

We will change the date on this page when the notice changes. The operator’s name and a contact address will be added here before launch.
